steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock.

steps.title: Access ACU and disconnect J3
steps.body: Remove the top panel to access the ACU. Disconnect connector J3 (wash heater) from the ACU.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove top panel to access machine electronics. Disconnect connector J3 from the ACU.

steps.title: Wash heater J3 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: With J3 disconnected at the ACU, measure resistance across pins 1 and 2. Expected 7–30 Ω at room temperature.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Using an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across pins 1 and 2 of connector J3. If the resistance is 7-30 Ω, the heating element and wiring are good.

steps.title: Access heating element
steps.body: Remove the back panel to access the heating element. Disconnect the wire connectors from the heating element terminals.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove back panel to access the heating element. Disconnect the wire connectors from the heating element.

steps.title: Heater ohms at element terminals
steps.body: Measure resistance across the two heating element terminals. Expected 7–30 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Using an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across the two heating element terminals. If the resistance is open, replace the heating element. If 7-30 Ω, replace the lower main harness.

branches.label: Open circuit (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element. Torque heater nut to 4.5 Nm ± 0.5 Nm on reinstall. Verify drum clearance after install.

branches.label: 7–30 Ω at element
branches.oemOutcome: Heating element is good — replace the lower main harness and retest with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Replace heating element
steps.oemOutcome: Replace heating element, torque nut 4.5 Nm ± 0.5 Nm, reassemble, and verify with Quick Service Cycle step 008.

steps.title: Replace lower main harness
steps.oemOutcome: Replace lower main harness between ACU and heater; reassemble and verify heat in Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Reconnect J3 and restore power
steps.body: Reinstall connector J3 on the ACU. Reassemble panels as needed. Plug in or restore power.

steps.title: Heater energizes during QSC step 008
steps.body: During Quick Service Cycle function 008 (Heater), does the wash heater turn on (tub warms / heater relay engages)?
steps.sourceExcerpt: 008 — Heater — Adds cold water to the drum, turns on heater. If heater does not turn on, see TEST #9: Wash Heating Element.

branches.label: Heater does not energize
branches.oemOutcome: Resistance was in range but heater did not energize — replace the ACU and retest with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Wash heater verified
steps.oemOutcome: Wash heater operates in Quick Service Cycle — reassemble and return washer to service.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.oemOutcome: If preceding steps did not correct the heating problem, replace the ACU and verify with Quick Service Cycle.
